h: Accepting Divine Kingship Builds the Sanctuary Above

p: In the holy Zohar (beginning of this parsha, III 2b):
"And Moshe was on the mountain, etc.,"
and it is written "And He called to Moshe";
which implies that Moshe was on Mount Sinai
at the time He called him;
yet it is written "from the Ohel Mo'ed,"
was not on Mount Sinai, etc.
the forty days were completed, etc.;
and one that rested on the Mishkan.
a cloud that shines and a cloud that is dark.
לְפִי פֵּירוּשׁ הַגָּהַת רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
according to the explanation of the gloss of Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory,
as the secret of the cloud of Malchus,
and "one that rested on the Mishkan"
is Malchus, the attribute of night,
for there are times the moon is covered,
and that is the dark cloud;
and the shining cloud is Binah,
as is written (in the holy Zohar III 4a),
with the utterance "Let there be light,"
for the pasuk 'And Moshe was on the mountain'
is at the end of Parshas Mishpatim,
and what connection does it have
to the parsha 'And He called to Moshe,
and spoke to him from the Ohel Mo'ed'?"
and he left it as needing study.
But in truth, in the holy Zohar's answer
that on the mountain there was an Ohel Mo'ed and a Mishkan,
and there was one cloud there
were said to Moshe at Sinai
and repeated in the Ohel Mo'ed;
and the entire book of Vayikra
even though this is not written,
as is written in Rashi's commentary;
and at the beginning of Parshas Behar
and its fine points were said from Sinai,
so too all of them," etc.
And why it singled out shemittah and yovel:
since these apply in Eretz Yisrael,
that they were said upon their entering the land,
that they were said at Sinai as well;
that general rules and details were said from Sinai.
And at the end of the parsha of rebukes
at Mount Sinai by the hand of Moshe";
and likewise at the end of the book of Vayikra

p: Now the whole matter of the korbanos
was not mentioned even in general terms,
רַק מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסוֹף פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ
except for what is said at the end of Parshas Yisro
and you shall sacrifice on it, etc.";
and only olos and shelamim are mentioned.
that the entire book of Vayikra
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י (סוֹטָה לז, ב)
And as is written in Rashi's commentary (Sotah 37b):
הַר סִינַי וְאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד חֲדָא הוּא
Mount Sinai and the Ohel Mo'ed are one,
that they were said at Sinai
and repeated in the Ohel Mo'ed.
Then why is there no hint
in the book of Toras Kohanim
except at the end of the book?
that the Mishkan was indeed on Mount Sinai.
And this is because at the splitting of the Sea
the Sanctuary, Hashem, which Your hands established";
וְאִלּוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כוּ׳
"whereas of the work of the hands of the tzaddikim, etc.,
And this is according to what Chazal said
a parable to a king, etc.;
from when You stood at the Sea
and we said song before You
hence "Your throne is established from Az,"
and the Beis HaMikdash is called
And the Beis HaMikdash was already built
through the deeds of the tzaddikim
who accepted the yoke of His kingship;
and this is why it says "Your hands established,"
because the Beis HaMikdash was already
And at the time of the giving of the Torah,
the Beis HaMikdash would have descended
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ל, א)
that the parshiyos were said in order,
were said during the first forty days,
not as is written in Rashi's commentary
(Ki Sisa, on the pasuk "And He gave to Moshe," Shemos 31:18),
that there is no chronological order in the Torah.
And so wrote the Ramban, of blessed memory,
and so it is explicit in the holy Zohar
And this is what it says in Parshas Terumah,
which was said to Moshe at Sinai:
כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מַרְאֶה אוֹתְךָ וְגוֹ׳
according to all that I show you, etc.";
and afterward in the section of the Menorah
which you are shown on the mountain";
and regarding the erection it is written (Shemos 26:30):
"And you shall erect the Mishkan according to its manner
which you were shown on the mountain";
had there not been the corruption
and they had not been broken,
Moshe Rabbeinu would have been Mashiach,
(קֹהֶלֶת א, ט) מַה שֶּׁהָיָה הוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה
(בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, י) עַד כִּי יָבוֹא שִׁילֹה
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמו, ב
וְתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן יח וְתִקּוּן סט)
and Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 18 and Tikkun 69).
And all the words of Torah would have been revealed,
as will be revealed in the future
and the Beis HaMikdash would have descended
and it is called the work of the hands of the tzaddikim,
by accepting the yoke of His kingship.
And this is what it says (Shemos 25:9):
and this is what is written in the holy Zohar
were all within the cloud," etc.
And so too with the Menorah,
which alludes to the Oral Torah,
as Chazal said (in Midrash Rabbah, Tetzaveh and Beha'alosecha):
it is written "And see and make according to their pattern, etc."
And likewise regarding the erection of the whole Mishkan
"according to its manner which you were shown, etc.":
for there the Beis HaMikdash was
from the splitting of the Sea,
And likewise with the copper altar it is written
"as He showed you on the mountain, etc.";
and as is written in the holy Zohar:
and what is written, "ruchin," is a scribal error);
that is, the pleasing fragrance of the korbanos.
the work of the hands of the tzaddikim,
that through their preparation they would merit
that it descend built and perfected.
alludes to the table of kings,
who was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus:
what is written in Parshas Mishpatim,
that is, the cloud that covered the Mishkan
and there was said to Moshe
the entire book of Toras Kohanim;
it was repeated in the Ohel Mo'ed in the wilderness,
and He spoke to him from the Ohel Mo'ed,"
to the Ohel Mo'ed that was on Mount Sinai.
עַל שֵׁם (שְׁמוֹת כה, כב) אֲשֶׁר אִוָּעֵד לְךָ
on account of (Shemos 25:22) "where I will meet with you,"
it was already called the Ohel Mo'ed,
for then there was the union
בֵּין קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
between HaKadosh Baruch Hu and Knesses Yisrael
from the splitting of the Sea,
and the heart of Yisrael became
And this is what it asked earlier,
that the Ohel Mo'ed was among Yisrael
that is, at the end of the forty days
the parshiyos of Terumah and Tetzaveh were said to him;
"And He called to Moshe from the Ohel Mo'ed."
That is, although Moshe was in the cloud
and one that rested on the Mishkan;
and He spoke to him from the Ohel Mo'ed."

p: 'And the glory of Hashem filled the Mishkan':
for it was complete above and below
if it were according to its simple sense,
that after the erection of the Mishkan
the glory of Hashem filled the Mishkan,
it means it was already full
which already filled the Mishkan above,
that had rested on the Mishkan since then,
And it refers also to the Mishkan below,
and this is what is said:
"for it was complete above and below
That is, the Mishkan above is Binah,
and it includes all the first three,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי ב, י)
in the manner of what it says (Mishlei 2:10):
and knowledge is pleasant to your soul";
and there the words of Torah were revealed
is from the attribute of Malchus;
as is written in the holy Zohar
(אִיּוֹב כח, יב) וְהַחָכְמָה מֵאַיִן תִּמָּצֵא כוּ׳
(Iyov 28:12) "And wisdom, from where will it be found?" etc.;
from the place called the Kodesh HaKodashim";
that the Kohen Gadol in the Kodesh HaKodashim
And this is the matter of the hidden Atika,
as is written (in the Idra Zuta, III 288b).
וְזֶהוּ כְּבוֹד ה׳ מָלֵא אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן
And this is "And the glory of Hashem filled the Mishkan,"
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וַיִּקְרָא אֶל מֹשֶׁה
and about this it says "And He called to Moshe,
all of Toras Kohanim at Mount Sinai;
and this is what it says at the end of the book:
אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹ׳
And according to the second intent,
"and Hashem spoke to him from the Ohel Mo'ed"
for it was repeated in the Ohel Mo'ed,
there is the spread shelter of peace
over us and over all His people Yisrael:
for although we have no Mikdash,
the yoke of His kingship, may He be blessed,
they merit the revelation of Atika Kadisha:
"the Sanctuary, Hashem, which Your hands established,"
עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂי יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים
through the work of the hands of the tzaddikim,
He ascended and sat on His throne of glory";
and the Ancient of Days sat";
and the heart becomes a Kodesh Kodashim

paragraphs.text: Source: Berachos 7a — “אמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי יוסי: מנין שהקדוש ברוך הוא מתפלל? שנאמר: ״והביאותים אל הר קדשי ושמחתים בבית תפלתי״, ״תפלתם״ לא נאמר, אלא ״תפלתי״, מכאן שהקדוש ברוך הוא מתפלל.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 118) — “Along the same lines, Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei: From where is it derived that the Holy One, Blessed be He, prays? As it is stated: “I will bring them to My holy mountain, and make them joyful in the house of My prayer” (Isaiah 56:7). The verse does not say the house of their prayer, but rather, “the house of My prayer”; from here we see that the Holy One, Blessed be He, prays.”
